summary: Repeat prompts slowed and intermittent 504s after KV-prefix cache eviction on dedicated pool
description: Issue summary: Several ScribeAI tenants on a dedicated GPU pool reported repeat-prompt latency regressions and intermittent 504 gateway timeouts when sending sequences of previously seen prompts (chat history + short system prefix). Impact: Customer-visible slowdowns for repeating prompts (token emission latency increased ~4-6x) and occasional request timeouts causing degraded UX and retries. Environment: prod-us-east, dedicated pool 'dedicated-us-east-42'. Observed start: 2026-03-13T13:10Z; correlated with autoscaler compaction and a config rollout to adjust prefix cache TTLs. Expected: Repeat prompts should be served from prefix/KV cache with sub-20ms amortized prefix retrieval; observed behavior shows full KV reload and serialization stalls on cache miss/eviction.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) On prod-us-east dedicated pool, send identical prompt+context pairs at t=0 and t=+30s using customer ScribeAI traffic pattern. 2) Observe average first-token latency for the second request. 3) Repeat with increased concurrency (10-20 parallel sessions). 4) Check serving-runtime / kv-cache metrics and logs for eviction/compaction events.
logs:
[2026-03-13T13:12:02Z] serving-runtime: prefix_cache: eviction event: reason=compaction threshold exceeded, freed=14MB, entries_evicted=312
[2026-03-13T13:12:02Z] router: req_id=abc123 path=/v1/chat model=redwood/fast-7b-v2 latency=812ms status=200
[2026-03-13T13:12:03Z] serving-runtime: kv-serializer: snapshot-serialize took=620ms keys=312
[2026-03-13T13:13:40Z] router: req_id=def456 path=/v1/chat model=redwood/fast-7b-v2 latency=5048ms status=504
[2026-03-13T13:14:10Z] autoscaler: pool=dedicated-us-east-42 compaction_triggered=true reason=memory-pressure
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: aggressive compaction/TTL change pushed earlier (config roll 2026-03-13T12:58Z) lowered prefix TTL and changed compaction thresholds; combined with a recently merged serializer change (commit ab12cd34ef) this caused long serialization pauses on eviction. Metrics show a spike in 'prefix_cache.evictions' and correlating spike in 'kv-serializer.serialize_ms'. Hot-path repro: when many small prefix keys are evicted, serializer consolidates them and blocks worker threads. We observed a cache key hash-clustering pattern causing disproportionate eviction of certain prefix namespaces (customer-specific prefixes). Additional signal: increased retries from upstream client leading to bursty warmup traffic, making eviction/warmup thrash worse.
resolution: Mitigations applied: 1) rolled back the TTL/compaction config change to previous stable values at 2026-03-13T14:05Z; 2) applied emergency patch to limit per-eviction serialization work (PR linked) and throttled serializer concurrency; 3) warmed hot-prefixes for affected customer via targeted pre-warm script. Customer-facing workaround: reduce concurrency and increase inter-request spacing for repeat prompts until warmup completes (~5 minutes). Long-term fix planned: PR #4520 to fix serializer batching logic, adjust compaction heuristics to respect namespace-aware quotas, and add instrumentation for per-prefix eviction impact. Deployment scheduled to staging 2026-03-15 and prod 2026-03-16 behind canary rollout.
